newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: At least 12 Shi'ites said killed in Kabul.
newsitem.headline: At least 12 Shi'ites said killed in Kabul.

text.p: At least 12 Shi'ite Moslems have been killed and mutilated in a southeastern district of the Afghan capital Kabul, U.N. sources said on Saturday.

They said a crowd gathered on Saturday to protest at the killings, which took place on Friday afternoon. Shots were fired as Islamic Taleban militiamen tried to disperse the protesters, two of whom were reported killed, the sources added.
The sources said the bodies of the murdered ethnic Hazara Shi'ites had been mutilated, but there was no immediate word on who had killed them or what the motive was.

The reported massacre follows fierce fighting earlier this week between Taleban militiamen and supporters of the pro-Iranian Shi'ite opposition Hezb-i-Wahdat militia backed by ethnic Uzbek fighters in the northern city of Mazar-i-Sharif.
The Taleban were driven out of the northern capital on Wednesday, just four days after they had entered it in a now-defunct alliance with Uzbeks led by General Abdul Malik.
The Hazara minority in Kabul is concentrated in two areas, the southwestern district of Karte Seh and Taimani in the north.
